content_voiceover: This flowchart walks through the ICC classification algorithm for MDS step by step, starting with blast percentage. The first decision point asks whether marrow or blood blasts fall in the 10 to 19 percent range. If yes, you move to the second decision point, which asks whether AML defining genes are present. If AML defining genes are present, the diagnosis is AML. If they are absent, the diagnosis is MDS slash AML. A side note lists three features that also route into this AML or MDS slash AML pathway even outside the strict blast percentage: T P 53 mutation, MDS related gene mutations, and MDS related cytogenetic abnormalities. If blasts are not in the 10 to 19 percent range, meaning they are lower, the algorithm asks whether multi hit T P 53 is present. If yes, the diagnosis is MDS with mutated T P 53. If multi hit T P 53 is absent, the algorithm checks marrow blasts of 5 to 9 percent or blood blasts of 2 to 9 percent. If that is satisfied, the diagnosis is MDS with excess blasts. This slide sets up the logic that continues on the next slide for the remaining, lower blast count categories.
keypoints: First branch point: are blasts 10 to 19 percent
AML defining genes present with 10 to 19 percent blasts equals AML
AML defining genes absent with 10 to 19 percent blasts equals MDS slash AML
Multi hit T P 53 at lower blast counts equals MDS with mutated T P 53
5 to 9 percent marrow or 2 to 9 percent blood blasts equals MDS with excess blasts
keypoint_voiceover: Walk the algorithm left to right. Blast percentage of 10 to 19 splits into AML versus MDS slash AML depending on AML defining genes. Below that range, multi hit T P 53 status is checked next, and only after that does the algorithm look at the 5 to 9 percent marrow or 2 to 9 percent blood blast threshold for MDS with excess blasts.
